title: Judging the Evidence for a Shorter Morning
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Judge the strength of the evidence behind eight claims about AI tutoring and the compressed morning, using the five evidence levels from Chapter 2.

educational.topic: Judging the Evidence for a Shorter Morning
learningObjectives: The learner will judge the strength of the evidence behind eight claims about AI tutoring and the compressed morning by assigning each to one of the five evidence levels from Chapter 2, correctly placing at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The five evidence levels, randomized controlled trial, and self-reported results, from Chapters 2 and 3
The studies described in the section "AI Tutors" in Chapter 11

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit an answer, get feedback with the reason, and review what was missed
commonMisconceptions: A famous or often-quoted result is strong evidence
A school's own reported gains are evidence of effect
A published meta-analysis is the same as a randomized trial
assessmentOpportunities: A school reports its own test gains with no comparison group. Which level?
Is a published meta-analysis the same as a randomized trial?
A tutor is built on solid research but has not been evaluated yet. Which level?

controls.name: Choice buttons
controls.description: commit an answer. A wrong first answer gives a hint and lets you choose again; only the first answer counts.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: opens or closes the reference table. Reading it is exploration, not evidence.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next item after feedback. On the results screen, Previous missed and Next missed step through what you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: starts a practice run with the items reshuffled. Practice runs do not change the first-run score.
